newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee continues to dip vs forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee continues to dip vs forward dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee continued to lose ground in the forward dollar market on Thursday, dealers said.
"There is paying pressure but we are not sure about the reasons," said a bank dealer in Bombay.

Some banks are said to be covering ahead of outward remittances for Haj pilgrims in the first quarter of calendar 1997. One dealer said some banks continued to liquidate their forward commitments in view of the firm call money rates.
Six month dollar spurted to 1.72/1.74 rupees at noon, up from the opening level of 1.67/1.70 rupees, dealers said.
The spot dollar market continued to be quiet, moving in a tight range in the absence of strong corporate dollar demand and the absence of a leading state-run bank from the market.
Dollar sales by Delhi-based banks also affected the sentiment, a dealer at a Bombay brokerage said.
"It (the rupee) can go up to 35.7450 if they come in," he said, referring to the state-run bank.
But there was no sign of it yet, he added.
The dollar was quoted at 35.710/720 in latest deals.
